records.Japanese:
ただ契約街を増やして航路を広げている
うちは、船を買う必要はありません
１％の契約では、買える交易品も
１つ～５つが限度ですからね
records.current_English:
You don't need more ships
 just to sign deals 
 with new towns 
 and open trade routes. 
 With a one percent share,
 you can buy only one to five units 
 of trade goods.
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.previous_English: You don't need more ships just to sign deals with new towns and open trade routes. With a one percent share, you can buy only one to five units of trade goods.
records.english: You can add towns to your trade routes without buying ships. A one percent share lets you buy just one to five units of goods.
protected_phrases: one to five units of goods.
records.source_meaning: New contracts and routes alone do not require new ships; a one-percent contract share buys only one to five units of goods.
records.context: Maria and her companions rescue Cesare from men he offended by correcting them about the shape of the Earth. Maria values his curiosity and ship knowledge and hires him as navigator. The script continues into his ship-buying advice without a text choice in this block.
records.localization_note: Cesare explains that opening up trade through more towns takes no new ship purchases yet. The one percent share and one-to-five-unit limit follow as a complete example.

A one percent share lets you buy
just one to five units of goods.

records.Japanese:
シェアが増えて
交易品がたくさん買えるようになったら
いよいよ船を買うときですね
records.current_English:
Once your market share grows 
 and you can buy more goods, it's 
 time to buy a ship.
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.previous_English: Once your market share grows and you can buy more goods, it's time to buy a ship.
records.english: Once your market share grows and you can buy more goods, it's time to buy a ship.
records.source_meaning: Larger shares and goods availability indicate it is time to buy ships.
records.context: Maria and her companions rescue Cesare from men he offended by correcting them about the shape of the Earth. Maria values his curiosity and ship knowledge and hires him as navigator. The script continues into his ship-buying advice without a text choice in this block.
records.localization_note: Keep the trigger for buying a ship tied to how much traders can buy as their share grows.

records.Japanese:
ここでまず考えるべきは
船の大きさと値段であります
records.current_English:
Start with the ship's
 size and price.
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.previous_English: Start with the ship's size and price.
records.english: Check the size and price first.
records.source_meaning: First consider a ship's size and price.
records.context: Maria and her companions rescue Cesare from men he offended by correcting them about the shape of the Earth. Maria values his curiosity and ship knowledge and hires him as navigator. The script continues into his ship-buying advice without a text choice in this block.
records.localization_note: Cesare has just said when to buy a ship. His next instruction names the two things to check first in one complete line.

lines: Check the size and price first.

records.Japanese:
シェアと所持金に応じた船を選ばな
ければ、船一杯に積めるだけの交易品を
買えないのに、結局、水夫ばかり
必要になってしまいます
records.current_English:
Buy a ship your market share 
 and budget can support.
 Otherwise you'll need more sailors 
 for a ship you can't fill.
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.previous_English: Buy a ship your market share and budget can support. Otherwise you'll need more sailors for a ship you can't fill.
records.english: Buy a ship your market share and budget can support. Otherwise you'll need more sailors for a ship you can't fill.
records.source_meaning: Match ships to shares and funds, or empty capacity will still require unnecessary sailors.
records.context: Maria and her companions rescue Cesare from men he offended by correcting them about the shape of the Earth. Maria values his curiosity and ship knowledge and hires him as navigator. The script continues into his ship-buying advice without a text choice in this block.
records.localization_note: The budget and market share both matter. The example shows why a ship too large to fill still costs sailors.

records.Japanese:
中型船には２本マストと３本マストが
あります。もちろん、３本マストの
ほうが速いのですが、操帆手が
多く必要になるのであります
records.current_English:
Medium ships 
 have two or three masts. 
 The ones with three are faster,
 but they need more sail handlers.
records.speaker: Cesare Tony
records.previous_English: Medium ships have two or three masts. The ones with three are faster, but they need more sail handlers.
records.english: Medium ships have 2 or 3 masts. Three make the ship faster, but you'll need more sail handlers.
records.source_meaning: Medium ships have two or three masts; three masts are faster but need more sail handlers.
records.context: Maria and her companions rescue Cesare from men he offended by correcting them about the shape of the Earth. Maria values his curiosity and ship knowledge and hires him as navigator. The script continues into his ship-buying advice without a text choice in this block.
records.localization_note: Lead with the two rig options on a complete line. Keep the higher speed and additional sail handlers attached to the three-mast option.

lines: but you'll need more sail handlers.

records.Japanese: 驚いたわ。そこまで見ていたとはね
records.current_English: Amazing. You picked up on all that.
records.speaker: Maria Li
records.previous_English: Amazing. You picked up on all that.
records.english: Amazing. You picked up on all that.
records.source_meaning: Maria is impressed by how much he noticed.
records.context: Maria can wager a drink, then win and see Fernando infer a couple's breakup. Xien challenges Fernando's claim of insight. Maria invites Fernando to join her company, and he answers by tossing a coin.
records.localization_note: Maria's surprise acknowledges the details Fernando caught and sets up his boast about reading people.

records.Japanese:
まあな、この洞察力があれば
相手の手をよむことができる
records.current_English:
Sure. Pick up on 
 things like that and you can read
 your opponent's moves.
records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.previous_English: Sure. Pick up on things like that and you can read your opponent's moves.
records.english: Sure. With an eye like mine, I can read my opponent's next move.
records.source_meaning: He says that perception lets him read an opponent's hand.
records.context: Maria can wager a drink, then win and see Fernando infer a couple's breakup. Xien challenges Fernando's claim of insight. Maria invites Fernando to join her company, and he answers by tossing a coin.
records.localization_note: Fernando boasts about his own ability to read a move, following the exact clues he noticed. Keep his confidence before he credits his luck.

lines: Sure. With an eye like mine,
I can read my opponent's next move.

records.Japanese:
後は俺の強運があれば
勝てるのさ
records.current_English: Add my luck to that, and I can win.
records.speaker: Fernando Dias
records.previous_English: Add my luck to that, and I can win.
records.english: Add my luck to that, and I can win.
records.source_meaning: Combined with his exceptional luck, it lets him win.
records.context: Maria can wager a drink, then win and see Fernando infer a couple's breakup. Xien challenges Fernando's claim of insight. Maria invites Fernando to join her company, and he answers by tossing a coin.
records.localization_note: Fernando gives luck the last word after explaining the skill he uses to read an opponent.

records.Japanese:
私のような船大工は、航海中に
『材木室』で傷ついた船を直します
造船所でも、船の改造や修理を
手伝いますよ
records.current_English:
At sea, shipwrights like me fix
 damage from the Lumber Room. 
 At the shipyard, we help 
 with refits and repairs.
records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.previous_English: At sea, shipwrights like me fix damage from the Lumber Room. At the shipyard, we help with refits and repairs.
records.english: At sea, shipwrights like me can repair damage in the Lumber Room. At the shipyard, we help with refits and repairs.
records.source_meaning: A carpenter like him repairs damaged ships at sea in the timber room and helps refitting and repairs at shipyards.
records.context: Xien spots Manuel admiring Maria's ship. Manuel's eye for its neglected maintenance impresses the pair. Maria invites him to return to life at sea, and he offers optional refit advice.
records.localization_note: Manuel identifies the Lumber Room as the work location for repairs at sea. His next sentence gives the work a shipwright can do at a shipyard.

lines: At sea, shipwrights like me can
repair damage in the Lumber Room.

records.Japanese:
駆け足の説明になりましたが…
参考になりましたかな？
records.current_English:
I went through that rather quickly.
 Did it help?
records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.previous_English: I went through that rather quickly. Did it help?
records.english: I went through that rather quickly. Did it help?
records.source_meaning: He hopes the hurried explanation proved useful.
records.context: Xien spots Manuel admiring Maria's ship. Manuel's eye for its neglected maintenance impresses the pair. Maria invites him to return to life at sea, and he offers optional refit advice.
records.localization_note: Manuel acknowledges his quick explanation and checks whether Maria found it useful.

records.Japanese:
艦隊の命運も、提督の采配次第です
船の改造も決しておろそかにせず
入念に行ってくださいよ
records.current_English:
The fleet's fate is in your hands, 
 Admiral. Don't neglect your refits.
 Plan them carefully.
records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.previous_English: The fleet's fate is in your hands, Admiral. Don't neglect your refits. Plan them carefully.
records.english: The fleet's fate is in your hands, Admiral. Don't neglect your refits. Plan them carefully.
records.source_meaning: The fleets fate depends on the admirals judgment; refit carefully rather than neglect it.
records.context: Xien spots Manuel admiring Maria's ship. Manuel's eye for its neglected maintenance impresses the pair. Maria invites him to return to life at sea, and he offers optional refit advice.
records.localization_note: Manuel closes the advice by putting responsibility for the fleet and careful refits in the admiral's hands.

records.Japanese:
そうですか
では、お任せしますよ
records.current_English:
I see. Then I'll 
 leave it in your hands.
records.speaker: Manuel Almeida
records.previous_English: I see. Then I'll leave it in your hands.
records.english: I see. I'll leave it to you, then.
records.source_meaning: On refusal he acknowledges the choice and leaves it to Maria.
